        User agents should ensure that the decoded media data stays readily available until at least the end of the next successful <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;update&#45;the&#45;rendering"></a>[update the rendering](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#update-the-rendering) step in the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;event&#45;loop"></a>[event loop](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-loop)&#46; This is an important part of the API contract&#44; and should not be broken if at all possible&#46; &#40;Typically&#44; this would only be violated in low&#45;memory situations that require evicting decoded image data&#44; or when the image is too large to keep in decoded form for this period of time&#46;&#41;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        Animated images will become <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;img&#45;all&#45;3"></a>[completely available](#img-all) only after all their frames are loaded&#46; Thus&#44; even though an implementation could decode the first frame before that point&#44; the above steps will not do so&#44; instead waiting until all frames are available&#46;

3.  Return <var>promise</var>&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Without the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;img&#45;decode&#45;2"></a><code>[decode&#40;&#41;](#dom-img-decode)</code> method&#44; the process of loading an <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;26"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element and then displaying it might look like the following&#58;

``` text
const img = new Image();
img.src = "nebula.jpg";
img.onload = () => {
    document.body.appendChild(img);
};
img.onerror = () => {
    document.body.appendChild(new Text("Could not load the nebula :("));
};
```

However&#44; this can cause notable dropped frames&#44; as the paint that occurs after inserting the image into the DOM causes a synchronous decode on the main thread&#46;

This can instead be rewritten using the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;img&#45;decode&#45;3"></a><code>[decode&#40;&#41;](#dom-img-decode)</code> method&#58;

``` text
const img = new Image();
img.src = "nebula.jpg";
img.decode().then(() => {
    document.body.appendChild(img);
}).catch(() => {
    document.body.appendChild(new Text("Could not load the nebula :("));
});
```

This latter form avoids the dropped frames of the original&#44; by allowing the user agent to decode the image <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;in&#45;parallel&#45;3"></a>[in parallel](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#in-parallel)&#44; and only inserting it into the DOM &#40;and thus causing it to be painted&#41; once the decoding process is complete&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Because the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;img&#45;decode&#45;4"></a><code>[decode&#40;&#41;](#dom-img-decode)</code> method attempts to ensure that the decoded image data is available for at least one frame&#44; it can be combined with the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;animationframeprovider&#45;requestanimationframe"></a><code>[requestAnimationFrame&#40;&#41;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-animationframeprovider-requestanimationframe)</code> API&#46; This means it can be used with coding styles or frameworks that ensure that all DOM modifications are batched together as <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;list&#45;of&#45;animation&#45;frame&#45;callbacks"></a>[animation frame callbacks](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#list-of-animation-frame-callbacks)&#58;

``` text
const container = document.querySelector("#container");

const { containerWidth, containerHeight } = computeDesiredSize();
requestAnimationFrame(() => {
 container.style.width = containerWidth;
 container.style.height = containerHeight;
});

// ...

const img = new Image();
img.src = "supernova.jpg";
img.decode().then(() => {
    requestAnimationFrame(() => container.appendChild(img));
});
```

A legacy factory function is provided for creating <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;htmlimageelement"></a><code>[HTMLImageElement](#htmlimageelement)</code> objects &#40;in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;createelement"></a><code>[createElement&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement)</code>&#41;&#58; <a id="dom&#45;image"></a><strong><code>Image&#40;<var>width</var>&#44; <var>height</var>&#41;</code></strong>&#46; When invoked&#44; the legacy factory function must perform the following steps&#58;

1.  Let <var>document</var> be the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;current&#45;global&#45;object"></a>[current global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#current-global-object)&#39;s <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;window"></a>[associated <code>Document</code>](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#concept-document-window)&#46;

2.  Let <var>img</var> be the result of <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;create&#45;an&#45;element"></a>[creating an element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element) given <var>document</var>&#44; &#34;<code>img</code>&#34;&#44; and the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#46;

3.  If <var>width</var> is given&#44; then <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;attributes&#45;set&#45;value"></a>[set an attribute value](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value) for <var>img</var> using &#34;<a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width&#45;5"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code>&#34; and <var>width</var>&#46;

4.  If <var>height</var> is given&#44; then <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;attributes&#45;set&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[set an attribute value](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-set-value) for <var>img</var> using &#34;<a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;height&#45;5"></a><code>[height](#attr-dim-height)</code>&#34; and <var>height</var>&#46;

5.  Return <var>img</var>&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A single image can have different appropriate alternative text depending on the context&#46;

In each of the following cases&#44; the same image is used&#44; yet the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;19"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> text is different each time&#46; The image is the coat of arms of the Carouge municipality in the canton Geneva in Switzerland&#46;

Here it is used as a supplementary icon&#58;

``` text
<p>I lived in <img src="carouge.svg" alt=""> Carouge.</p>
```

Here it is used as an icon representing the town&#58;

``` text
<p>Home town: <img src="carouge.svg" alt="Carouge"></p>
```

Here it is used as part of a text on the town&#58;

``` text
<p>Carouge has a coat of arms.</p>
<p><img src="carouge.svg" alt="The coat of arms depicts a lion, sitting in front of a tree."></p>
<p>It is used as decoration all over the town.</p>
```

Here it is used as a way to support a similar text where the description is given as well as&#44; instead of as an alternative to&#44; the image&#58;

``` text
<p>Carouge has a coat of arms.</p>
<p><img src="carouge.svg" alt=""></p>
<p>The coat of arms depicts a lion, sitting in front of a tree.
It is used as decoration all over the town.</p>
```

Here it is used as part of a story&#58;

``` text
<p>She picked up the folder and a piece of paper fell out.</p>
<p><img src="carouge.svg" alt="Shaped like a shield, the paper had a
red background, a green tree, and a yellow lion with its tongue
hanging out and whose tail was shaped like an S."></p>
<p>She stared at the folder. S! The answer she had been looking for all
this time was simply the letter S! How had she not seen that before? It all
came together now. The phone call where Hector had referred to a lion's tail,
the time Maria had stuck her tongue out...</p>
```

Here it is not known at the time of publication what the image will be&#44; only that it will be a coat of arms of some kind&#44; and thus no replacement text can be provided&#44; and instead only a brief caption for the image is provided&#44; in the <a id="the&#45;img&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;title&#45;3"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute&#58;

``` text
<p>The last user to have uploaded a coat of arms uploaded this one:</p>
<p><img src="last-uploaded-coat-of-arms.cgi" title="User-uploaded coat of arms."></p>
```

Ideally&#44; the author would find a way to provide real replacement text even in this case&#44; e&#46;g&#46; by asking the previous user&#46; Not providing replacement text makes the document more difficult to use for people who are unable to view images&#44; e&#46;g&#46; blind users&#44; or users or very low&#45;bandwidth connections or who pay by the byte&#44; or users who are forced to use a text&#45;only web browser&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here are some more examples showing the same picture used in different contexts&#44; with different appropriate alternate texts each time&#46;

``` text
<article>
 <h1>My cats</h1>
 <h2>Fluffy</h2>
 <p>Fluffy is my favorite.</p>
 <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="She likes playing with a ball of yarn.">
 <p>She's just too cute.</p>
 <h2>Miles</h2>
 <p>My other cat, Miles just eats and sleeps.</p>
</article>
```

``` text
<article>
 <h1>Photography</h1>
 <h2>Shooting moving targets indoors</h2>
 <p>The trick here is to know how to anticipate; to know at what speed and
 what distance the subject will pass by.</p>
 <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="A cat flying by, chasing a ball of yarn, can be
 photographed quite nicely using this technique.">
 <h2>Nature by night</h2>
 <p>To achieve this, you'll need either an extremely sensitive film, or
 immense flash lights.</p>
</article>
```

``` text
<article>
 <h1>About me</h1>
 <h2>My pets</h2>
 <p>I've got a cat named Fluffy and a dog named Miles.</p>
 <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="Fluffy, my cat, tends to keep itself busy.">
 <p>My dog Miles and I like go on long walks together.</p>
 <h2>music</h2>
 <p>After our walks, having emptied my mind, I like listening to Bach.</p>
</article>
```

``` text
<article>
 <h1>Fluffy and the Yarn</h1>
 <p>Fluffy was a cat who liked to play with yarn. She also liked to jump.</p>
 <aside><img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="" title="Fluffy"></aside>
 <p>She would play in the morning, she would play in the evening.</p>
</article>
```

#### <a id="images"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4 Images[](#images)

##### <a id="introduction&#45;3"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;1 Introduction[](#introduction-3)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

To embed an image in HTML&#44; when there is only a single image resource&#44; use the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element and its <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

``` text
<h2>From today's featured article</h2>
<img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg" alt="" width="100" height="150">
<p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
```

However&#44; there are a number of situations for which the author might wish to use multiple image resources that the user agent can choose from&#58;

- Different users might have different environmental characteristics&#58;

  - The users&#39; physical screen size might be different from one another&#46;

    <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

    A mobile phone&#39;s screen might be 4 inches diagonally&#44; while a laptop&#39;s screen might be 14 inches diagonally&#46;

    <svg font-size="2.5" role="img" viewbox="0 0 80 32" font-family="sans-serif" height="200" aria-label="The phone's screen is much smaller compared to the laptop's screen.">                  <rect rx="1" x="6" y="18" stroke="black" width="6" fill="white" height="12"></rect>         <text transform="translate(9 24)         rotate(-60)" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">4″</text>                  <rect y="2" stroke="black" width="40" stroke-width="2" fill="white" height="26" rx="2" x="30"></rect>         <line y1="30" y2="30" stroke-width="2" stroke="black" x1="26" stroke-linecap="round" x2="74"></line>         <text transform="translate(50 15)         rotate(-30)" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">14″</text>        </svg>

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    This is only relevant when an image&#39;s rendered size depends on the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) size&#46;

  - The users&#39; screen pixel density might be different from one another&#46;

    <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

    A mobile phone&#39;s screen might have three times as many physical pixels per inch compared to another mobile phone&#39;s screen&#44; regardless of their physical screen size&#46;

    <svg font-size="2.5" role="img" viewbox="0 0 56 27" font-family="sans-serif" height="170" aria-label="One phone has big pixels, the other has small pixels.">         <defs>          <pattern x="0" y="0" id="img-intro-pixel" width="3" patternunits="userSpaceOnUse" height="3" stroke-linecap="round">           <rect x="0" y="0" fill="black" width="3" height="3"></rect>           <line x1="0.5" x2="0.5" stroke="red" y1="0.5" y2="2.5"></line>           <line x1="1.5" x2="1.5" stroke="lime" y1="0.5" y2="2.5"></line>           <line x1="2.5" x2="2.5" stroke="blue" y1="0.5" y2="2.5"></line>          </pattern>         </defs>                  <rect rx="1" x="6" y="8" stroke="black" width="6" fill="white" height="12"></rect>         <rect rx="1" x="36" y="8" stroke="black" width="6" fill="white" height="12"></rect>                  <line y2="24" stroke-width="3" stroke="brown" x1="15" x2="22" y1="16"></line>         <circle fill="url(#img-intro-pixel)" stroke="black" cx="10" r="8" cy="10"></circle>         <line y2="24" stroke-width="3" stroke="brown" x1="45" x2="52" y1="16"></line>         <circle stroke-width="3" stroke="black" fill="url(#img-intro-pixel)" cx="120" r="24" cy="30" transform="scale(0.333333)"></circle>                  <text x="20" y="10" dominant-baseline="middle">1x</text>         <text x="50" y="10" dominant-baseline="middle">3x</text>        </svg>

  - The users&#39; zoom level might be different from one another&#44; or might change for a single user over time&#46;

    <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

    A user might zoom in to a particular image to be able to get a more detailed look&#46;

    The zoom level and the screen pixel density &#40;the previous point&#41; can both affect the number of physical screen pixels per <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;&#39;px&#39;"></a>[CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)&#46; This ratio is usually referred to as <a id="device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio"></a><strong>device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio</strong>&#46;

  - The users&#39; screen orientation might be different from one another&#44; or might change for a single user over time&#46;

    <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

    A tablet can be held upright or rotated 90 degrees&#44; so that the screen is either &#34;portrait&#34; or &#34;landscape&#34;&#46;

    <svg font-size="2.5" role="img" viewbox="0 0 60 32" font-family="sans-serif" height="200" aria-label="The tablet has two orientations.">                  <rect rx="1" x="6" y="5" stroke="black" width="14" fill="white" height="20"></rect>         <line y2="24" stroke-width="1.1" stroke="black" x1="6" x2="20" y1="24"></line>         <text text-anchor="middle" x="13" y="14.5" dominant-baseline="middle">Portrait</text>         <rect rx="1" x="30" y="11" stroke="black" width="20" fill="white" height="14"></rect>         <line y2="11" stroke-width="1.1" stroke="black" x1="31" x2="31" y1="25"></line>         <text text-anchor="middle" x="40.5" y="18" dominant-baseline="middle">Landscape</text>        </svg>

  - The users&#39; network speed&#44; network latency and bandwidth cost might be different from one another&#44; or might change for a single user over time&#46;

    <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

    A user might be on a fast&#44; low&#45;latency and constant&#45;cost connection while at work&#44; on a slow&#44; low&#45;latency and constant&#45;cost connection while at home&#44; and on a variable&#45;speed&#44; high&#45;latency and variable&#45;cost connection anywhere else&#46;

- Authors might want to show the same image content but with different rendered size depending on&#44; usually&#44; the width of the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;2"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#46; This is usually referred to as <a id="viewport&#45;based&#45;selection"></a><strong>viewport&#45;based selection</strong>&#46;

  <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

  A web page might have a banner at the top that always spans the entire <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;3"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width&#46; In this case&#44; the rendered size of the image depends on the physical size of the screen &#40;assuming a maximised browser window&#41;&#46;

  <svg aria-label="The upright-held phone shows a      small wolf at the top, and the tablet shows the same image but it is bigger." role="img" height="160" viewbox="0 0 52 25.6">                      <rect rx="1" x="6" y="8" stroke="black" width="6" fill="white" height="12"></rect>       <rect x="7" y="9" fill="#716966" width="4" height="2"></rect>       <image x="7" y="9" width="4" xlink:href="/images/wolf.jpg" height="2"></image>               <rect rx="1" x="25" y="6" stroke="black" width="20" fill="white" height="14"></rect>       <line y2="6" stroke-width="1.1" stroke="black" x1="26" x2="26" y1="20"></line>       <rect x="27" y="7" fill="#716966" width="17" height="8.5"></rect>       <image x="27" y="7" width="17" xlink:href="/images/wolf.jpg" height="8.5"></image>       </svg>

  <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

  Another web page might have images in columns&#44; with a single column for screens with a small physical size&#44; two columns for screens with medium physical size&#44; and three columns for screens with big physical size&#44; with the images varying in rendered size in each case to fill up the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;4"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#46; In this case&#44; the rendered size of an image might be <em>bigger</em> in the one&#45;column layout compared to the two&#45;column layout&#44; despite the screen being smaller&#46;

  <svg font-size="2.5" role="img" viewbox="0 0 115 32" font-family="sans-serif" height="200" aria-label="The rotated phone shows a top part of an image of a kettlebell swing; the      upright-held tablet shows a bit smaller images in two columns; the laptop shows images in three      columns.">                      <rect rx="1" x="6" y="24" stroke="black" width="12" fill="white" height="6"></rect>       <rect x="7" y="25" fill="#987b5a" width="10" height="4.5"></rect>       <image xlink:href="/images/kettlebell.jpg" preserveaspectratio="xMinYMin slice" width="10" x="7" height="4.5" y="25"></image>       <text text-anchor="middle" x="12" y="21">Narrow, 1 column</text>               <rect rx="1" x="32" y="10" stroke="black" width="14" fill="white" height="20"></rect>       <line y2="29" stroke-width="1.1" stroke="black" x1="32" x2="46" y1="29"></line>       <rect x="33" y="11" fill="#987b5a" width="5.5" height="5.5"></rect>       <image x="33" y="11" width="5.5" xlink:href="/images/kettlebell.jpg" height="5.5"></image>       <rect x="39.5" y="11" fill="burlywood" width="5.5" height="5.5"></rect>       <rect x="33" y="17.5" fill="silver" width="5.5" height="5.5"></rect>       <text text-anchor="middle" x="39" y="7">Medium, 2 columns</text>               <rect y="2" stroke="black" width="40" stroke-width="2" fill="white" height="26" rx="2" x="65"></rect>       <line y1="30" y2="30" stroke-width="2" stroke="black" x1="61" stroke-linecap="round" x2="109"></line>       <rect x="67" y="4" fill="#987b5a" width="10" height="10"></rect>       <image x="67" y="4" width="10" xlink:href="/images/kettlebell.jpg" height="10"></image>       <rect x="80" y="4" fill="burlywood" width="10" height="10"></rect>       <rect x="93" y="4" fill="silver" width="10" height="10"></rect>       <text text-anchor="middle" x="85" y="25">Wide, 3 columns</text>      </svg>

- Authors might want to show different image content depending on the rendered size of the image&#46; This is usually referred to as <a id="art&#45;direction"></a><strong>art direction</strong>&#46;

  <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

  When a web page is viewed on a screen with a large physical size &#40;assuming a maximised browser window&#41;&#44; the author might wish to include some less relevant parts surrounding the critical part of the image&#46; When the same web page is viewed on a screen with a small physical size&#44; the author might wish to show only the critical part of the image&#46;

  <svg aria-label="The upright-held phone shows a      cropped image of a wolf; the rotated tablet shows the uncropped image." role="img" height="160" viewbox="0 0 52 25.6">                      <rect rx="1" x="6" y="8" stroke="black" width="6" fill="white" height="12"></rect>       <rect x="7" y="9" fill="#716966" width="4" height="6"></rect>       <image xlink:href="/images/wolf.jpg" preserveaspectratio="xMidYMid slice" width="4" x="7" height="6" y="9"></image>               <rect rx="1" x="25" y="6" stroke="black" width="20" fill="white" height="14"></rect>       <line y2="6" stroke-width="1.1" stroke="black" x1="26" x2="26" y1="20"></line>       <rect x="27" y="7" fill="#716966" width="17" height="8.5"></rect>       <image x="27" y="7" width="17" xlink:href="/images/wolf.jpg" height="8.5"></image>       </svg>

- Authors might want to show the same image content but using different image formats&#44; depending on which image formats the user agent supports&#46; This is usually referred to as <a id="image&#45;format&#45;based&#45;selection"></a><strong>image format&#45;based selection</strong>&#46;

  <strong>Example&#58;</strong>

  A web page might have some images in the JPEG&#44; WebP and JPEG XR image formats&#44; with the latter two having better compression abilities compared to JPEG&#46; Since different user agents can support different image formats&#44; with some formats offering better compression ratios&#44; the author would like to serve the better formats to user agents that support them&#44; while providing JPEG fallback for user agents that don&#39;t&#46;

The above situations are not mutually exclusive&#46; For example&#44; it is reasonable to combine different resources for different <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio"></a>[device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio](#device-pixel-ratio) with different resources for <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;art&#45;direction"></a>[art direction](#art-direction)&#46;

While it is possible to solve these problems using scripting&#44; doing so introduces some other problems&#58;

- Some user agents aggressively download images specified in the HTML markup&#44; before scripts have had a chance to run&#44; so that web pages complete loading sooner&#46; If a script changes which image to download&#44; the user agent will potentially start two separate downloads&#44; which can instead cause worse page loading performance&#46;

- If the author avoids specifying any image in the HTML markup and instead instantiates a single download from script&#44; that avoids the double download problem above but then no image will be downloaded at all for users with scripting disabled and the aggressive image downloading optimization will also be disabled&#46;

With this in mind&#44; this specification introduces a number of features to address the above problems in a declarative manner&#46;

<strong><a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio&#45;2"></a>[Device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio](#device-pixel-ratio)&#45;based selection when the rendered size of the image is fixed</strong>

The <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;2"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> and <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> attributes on the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element can be used&#44; using the <code>x</code> descriptor&#44; to provide multiple images that only vary in their size &#40;the smaller image is a scaled&#45;down version of the bigger image&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <code>x</code> descriptor is not appropriate when the rendered size of the image depends on the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;5"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width &#40;<a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;based&#45;selection"></a>[viewport&#45;based selection](#viewport-based-selection)&#41;&#44; but can be used together with <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;art&#45;direction&#45;2"></a>[art direction](#art-direction)&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

``` text
<h2>From today's featured article</h2>
<img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg"
     srcset="/uploads/150-marie-lloyd.jpg 1.5x, /uploads/200-marie-lloyd.jpg 2x"
     alt="" width="100" height="150">
<p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
```

The user agent can choose any of the given resources depending on the user&#39;s screen&#39;s pixel density&#44; zoom level&#44; and possibly other factors such as the user&#39;s network conditions&#46;

For backwards compatibility with older user agents that don&#39;t yet understand the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset&#45;2"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> attribute&#44; one of the URLs is specified in the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;3"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#46; This will result in something useful &#40;though perhaps lower&#45;resolution than the user would like&#41; being displayed even in older user agents&#46; For new user agents&#44; the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;4"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute participates in the resource selection&#44; as if it was specified in <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset&#45;3"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> with a <code>1x</code> descriptor&#46;

The image&#39;s rendered size is given in the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code> and <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;height"></a><code>[height](#attr-dim-height)</code> attributes&#44; which allows the user agent to allocate space for the image before it is downloaded&#46;

<strong><a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;based&#45;selection&#45;2"></a>[Viewport&#45;based selection](#viewport-based-selection)</strong>

The <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset&#45;4"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> and <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attributes can be used&#44; using the <code>w</code> descriptor&#44; to provide multiple images that only vary in their size &#40;the smaller image is a scaled&#45;down version of the bigger image&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example&#44; a banner image takes up the entire <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;6"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width &#40;using appropriate CSS&#41;&#46;

``` text
<h1><img sizes="100vw" srcset="wolf-400.jpg 400w, wolf-800.jpg 800w, wolf-1600.jpg 1600w"
     src="wolf-400.jpg" alt="The rad wolf"></h1>
```

The user agent will calculate the effective pixel density of each image from the specified <code>w</code> descriptors and the specified rendered size in the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;2"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute&#46; It can then choose any of the given resources depending on the user&#39;s screen&#39;s pixel density&#44; zoom level&#44; and possibly other factors such as the user&#39;s network conditions&#46;

If the user&#39;s screen is 320 <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;&#39;px&#39;&#45;2"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide&#44; this is equivalent to specifying <code>wolf&#45;400&#46;jpg 1&#46;25x&#44; wolf&#45;800&#46;jpg 2&#46;5x&#44; wolf&#45;1600&#46;jpg 5x</code>&#46; On the other hand&#44; if the user&#39;s screen is 1200 <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;&#39;px&#39;&#45;3"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide&#44; this is equivalent to specifying <code>wolf&#45;400&#46;jpg 0&#46;33x&#44; wolf&#45;800&#46;jpg 0&#46;67x&#44; wolf&#45;1600&#46;jpg 1&#46;33x</code>&#46; By using the <code>w</code> descriptors and the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;3"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute&#44; the user agent can choose the correct image source to download regardless of how large the user&#39;s device is&#46;

For backwards compatibility&#44; one of the URLs is specified in the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;5"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#46; In new user agents&#44; the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;6"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute is ignored when the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset&#45;5"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> attribute uses <code>w</code> descriptors&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example&#44; the web page has three layouts depending on the width of the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;7"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#46; The narrow layout has one column of images &#40;the width of each image is about 100&#37;&#41;&#44; the middle layout has two columns of images &#40;the width of each image is about 50&#37;&#41;&#44; and the widest layout has three columns of images&#44; and some page margin &#40;the width of each image is about 33&#37;&#41;&#46; It breaks between these layouts when the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;8"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) is <code>30em</code> wide and <code>50em</code> wide&#44; respectively&#46;

``` text
<img sizes="(max-width: 30em) 100vw, (max-width: 50em) 50vw, calc(33vw - 100px)"
     srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
     src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
```

The <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;4"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute sets up the layout breakpoints at <code>30em</code> and <code>50em</code>&#44; and declares the image sizes between these breakpoints to be <code>100vw</code>&#44; <code>50vw</code>&#44; or <code>calc&#40;33vw &#45; 100px&#41;</code>&#46; These sizes do not necessarily have to match up exactly with the actual image width as specified in the CSS&#46;

The user agent will pick a width from the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;5"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute&#44; using the first item with a <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;media&#45;condition"></a>[&#60;media&#45;condition&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition) &#40;the part in parentheses&#41; that evaluates to true&#44; or using the last item &#40;<code>calc&#40;33vw &#45; 100px&#41;</code>&#41; if they all evaluate to false&#46;

For example&#44; if the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;9"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width is <code>29em</code>&#44; then <code>&#40;max&#45;width&#58; 30em&#41;</code> evaluates to true and <code>100vw</code> is used&#44; so the image size&#44; for the purpose of resource selection&#44; is <code>29em</code>&#46; If the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;10"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width is instead <code>32em</code>&#44; then <code>&#40;max&#45;width&#58; 30em&#41;</code> evaluates to false&#44; but <code>&#40;max&#45;width&#58; 50em&#41;</code> evaluates to true and <code>50vw</code> is used&#44; so the image size&#44; for the purpose of resource selection&#44; is <code>16em</code> &#40;half the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;11"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width&#41;&#46; Notice that the slightly wider <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;12"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) results in a smaller image because of the different layout&#46;

The user agent can then calculate the effective pixel density and choose an appropriate resource similarly to the previous example&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This example is the same as the previous example&#44; but the image is <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;loading&#45;lazy&#45;state"></a>[lazy&#45;loaded](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-loading-lazy-state)&#46; In this case&#44; the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;6"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute can use the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> keyword&#44; and the user agent will use the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width&#45;2"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code> attribute &#40;or the width specified in CSS&#41; for the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2)&#46;

``` text
<img loading="lazy" width="200" height="200" sizes="auto"
     srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
     src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
```

For better backwards&#45;compatibility with legacy user agents that don&#39;t support the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;2"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> keyword&#44; fallback sizes can be specified if desired&#46;

``` text
<img loading="lazy" width="200" height="200"
     sizes="auto, (max-width: 30em) 100vw, (max-width: 50em) 50vw, calc(33vw - 100px)"
     srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
     src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
```

<strong><a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;art&#45;direction&#45;3"></a>[Art direction](#art-direction)&#45;based selection</strong>

The <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code> element and the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element&#44; together with the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;media"></a><code>[media](#attr-source-media)</code> attribute&#44; can be used to provide multiple images that vary the image content &#40;for instance the smaller image might be a cropped version of the bigger image&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

``` text
<picture>
  <source media="(min-width: 45em)" srcset="large.jpg">
  <source media="(min-width: 32em)" srcset="med.jpg">
  <img src="small.jpg" alt="The wolf runs through the snow.">
</picture>
```

The user agent will choose the first <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element for which the media query in the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;media&#45;2"></a><code>[media](#attr-source-media)</code> attribute matches&#44; and then choose an appropriate URL from its <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;srcset"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-source-srcset)</code> attribute&#46;

The rendered size of the image varies depending on which resource is chosen&#46; To specify dimensions that the user agent can use before having downloaded the image&#44; CSS can be used&#46;

``` text
img { width: 300px; height: 300px }
@media (min-width: 32em) { img { width: 500px; height:300px } }
@media (min-width: 45em) { img { width: 700px; height:400px } }
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This example combines <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;art&#45;direction&#45;4"></a>[art direction](#art-direction)&#45; and <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio&#45;3"></a>[device&#45;pixel&#45;ratio](#device-pixel-ratio)&#45;based selection&#46; A banner that takes half the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;viewport&#45;13"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) is provided in two versions&#44; one for wide screens and one for narrow screens&#46;

``` text
<h1>
 <picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 500px)" srcset="banner-phone.jpeg, banner-phone-HD.jpeg 2x">
  <img src="banner.jpeg" srcset="banner-HD.jpeg 2x" alt="The Breakfast Combo">
 </picture>
</h1>
```

<strong><a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;image&#45;format&#45;based&#45;selection"></a>[Image format&#45;based selection](#image-format-based-selection)</strong>

The <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-source-type)</code> attribute on the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element can be used to provide multiple images in different formats&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

``` text
<h2>From today's featured article</h2>
<picture>
 <source srcset="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.webp" type="image/webp">
 <source srcset="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jxr" type="image/vnd.ms-photo">
 <img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg" alt="" width="100" height="150">
</picture>
<p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
```

In this example&#44; the user agent will choose the first source that has a <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;type&#45;2"></a><code>[type](#attr-source-type)</code> attribute with a supported MIME type&#46; If the user agent supports WebP images&#44; the first <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element will be chosen&#46; If not&#44; but the user agent does support JPEG XR images&#44; the second <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element will be chosen&#46; If neither of those formats are supported&#44; the <a id="introduction&#45;3&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element will be chosen&#46;

###### <a id="adaptive&#45;images"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;1&#46;1 Adaptive images[](#adaptive-images)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

CSS and media queries can be used to construct graphical page layouts that adapt dynamically to the user&#39;s environment&#44; in particular to different <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) dimensions and pixel densities&#46; For content&#44; however&#44; CSS does not help&#59; instead&#44; we have the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> attribute and the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code> element&#46; This section walks through a sample case showing how to use these features&#46;

Consider a situation where on wide screens &#40;wider than 600 <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;&#39;px&#39;"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)&#41; a 300×150 image named <code>a&#45;rectangle&#46;png</code> is to be used&#44; but on smaller screens &#40;600 <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;&#39;px&#39;&#45;2"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) and less&#41;&#44; a smaller 100×100 image called <code>a&#45;square&#46;png</code> is to be used&#46; The markup for this would look like this&#58;

``` text
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses.">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>
```

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

For details on what to put in the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#44; see the [Requirements for providing text to act as an alternative for images](#alt) section&#46;

The problem with this is that the user agent does not necessarily know what dimensions to use for the image when the image is loading&#46; To avoid the layout having to be reflowed multiple times as the page is loading&#44; CSS and CSS media queries can be used to provide the dimensions&#58;

``` text
<style>
 #a { width: 300px; height: 150px; }
 @media (max-width: 600px) { #a { width: 100px; height: 100px; } }
</style>
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses." id="a">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>
```

Alternatively&#44; the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code> and <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;height"></a><code>[height](#attr-dim-height)</code> attributes can be used on the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> and <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> elements to provide the width and height&#58;

``` text
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)" width="100" height="100">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" width="300" height="150"
  alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses.">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element is used with the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#44; which gives the URL of the image to use for legacy user agents that do not support the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code> element&#46; This leads to a question of which image to provide in the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;2"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#46;

If the author wants the biggest image in legacy user agents&#44; the markup could be as follows&#58;

``` text
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <img src="pear-desktop.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

However&#44; if legacy mobile user agents are more important&#44; one can list all three images in the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> elements&#44; overriding the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;3"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute entirely&#46;

``` text
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg">
 <img src="pear-mobile.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

Since at this point the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;4"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute is actually being ignored entirely by <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code>&#45;supporting user agents&#44; the <a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src&#45;5"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute can default to any image&#44; including one that is neither the smallest nor biggest&#58;

``` text
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg">
 <img src="pear-tablet.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Above the <code>max&#45;width</code> media feature is used&#44; giving the maximum &#40;<a id="adaptive&#45;images&#58;viewport&#45;2"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#41; dimensions that an image is intended for&#46; It is also possible to use <code>min&#45;width</code> instead&#46;

``` text
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg" media="(min-width: 1281px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(min-width: 721px)">
 <img src="pear-mobile.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

##### <a id="attributes&#45;common&#45;to&#45;source&#45;and&#45;img&#45;elements"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;2 Attributes common to <a id="attributes&#45;common&#45;to&#45;source&#45;and&#45;img&#45;elements&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code>&#44; <a id="attributes&#45;common&#45;to&#45;source&#45;and&#45;img&#45;elements&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code>&#44; and <a id="attributes&#45;common&#45;to&#45;source&#45;and&#45;img&#45;elements&#58;the&#45;link&#45;element"></a><code>[link](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-link-element)</code> elements[](#attributes-common-to-source-and-img-elements)

###### <a id="srcset&#45;attributes"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;2&#46;1 Srcset attributes[](#srcset-attributes)

A <a id="srcset&#45;attribute"></a><strong>srcset attribute</strong> is an attribute with requirements defined in this section&#46;

If present&#44; its value must consist of one or more <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string"></a>[image candidate strings](#image-candidate-string)&#44; each separated from the next by a U&#43;002C COMMA character &#40;&#44;&#41;&#46; If an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;2"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) contains no descriptors and no <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace) after the URL&#44; the following <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;3"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string)&#44; if there is one&#44; must begin with one or more <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;

An <a id="image&#45;candidate&#45;string"></a><strong>image candidate string</strong> consists of the following components&#44; in order&#44; with the further restrictions described below this list&#58;

1.  Zero or more <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;3"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;

2.  A <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;empty&#45;url"></a>[valid non&#45;empty URL](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-non-empty-url) that does not start or end with a U&#43;002C COMMA character &#40;&#44;&#41;&#44; referencing a non&#45;interactive&#44; optionally animated&#44; image resource that is neither paged nor scripted&#46;

3.  Zero or more <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;4"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;

4.  Zero or one of the following&#58;

    - A <a id="width&#45;descriptor"></a><strong>width descriptor</strong>&#44; consisting of&#58; <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;5"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; a <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer"></a>[valid non&#45;negative integer](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-non-negative-integer) giving a number greater than zero representing the <a id="width&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a><strong>width descriptor value</strong>&#44; and a U&#43;0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character&#46;

    - A <a id="pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor"></a><strong>pixel density descriptor</strong>&#44; consisting of&#58; <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;6"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; a <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-floating-point-number) giving a number greater than zero representing the <a id="pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a><strong>pixel density descriptor value</strong>&#44; and a U&#43;0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character&#46;

5.  Zero or more <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;7"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;

There must not be an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;4"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) for an element that has the same <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a>[width descriptor value](#width-descriptor-value) as another <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;5"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string)&#39;s <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[width descriptor value](#width-descriptor-value) for the same element&#46;

There must not be an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;6"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) for an element that has the same <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a>[pixel density descriptor value](#pixel-density-descriptor-value) as another <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;7"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string)&#39;s <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[pixel density descriptor value](#pixel-density-descriptor-value) for the same element&#46; For the purpose of this requirement&#44; an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;8"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) with no descriptors is equivalent to an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;9"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) with a <code>1x</code> descriptor&#46;

If an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;10"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string) for an element has the <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor) specified&#44; all other <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;11"></a>[image candidate strings](#image-candidate-string) for that element must also have the <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;2"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor) specified&#46;

The specified width in an <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;12"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string)&#39;s <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;3"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor) must match the <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;natural&#45;width"></a>[natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) in the resource given by the <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;13"></a>[image candidate string](#image-candidate-string)&#39;s URL&#44; if it has a <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;natural&#45;width&#45;2"></a>[natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width)&#46;

If an element has a <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;sizes&#45;attribute"></a>[sizes attribute](#sizes-attribute) present&#44; all <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;image&#45;candidate&#45;string&#45;14"></a>[image candidate strings](#image-candidate-string) for that element must have the <a id="srcset&#45;attributes&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;4"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor) specified&#46;

###### <a id="sizes&#45;attributes"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;2&#46;2 Sizes attributes[](#sizes-attributes)

A <a id="sizes&#45;attribute"></a><strong>sizes attribute</strong> is an attribute with requirements defined in this section&#46;

If present&#44; the value must be a <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valid&#45;source&#45;size&#45;list"></a>[valid source size list](#valid-source-size-list)&#46;

A <a id="valid&#45;source&#45;size&#45;list"></a><strong>valid source size list</strong> is a string that matches the following grammar&#58; [&#91;CSSVALUES&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSVALUES) [&#91;MQ&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsMQ)

<a id="source&#45;size&#45;list"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value"></a><a id="source&#45;size"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;media&#45;condition"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value&#45;2"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto"></a><a id="source&#45;size&#45;value"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;length&#45;2"></a><a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;2"></a>

``` text
<source-size-list> = <source-size>#? , <source-size-value>
<source-size> = <media-condition> <source-size-value> | auto
<source-size-value> = <length> | auto
```

A <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value) that is a <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;length&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[&#60;length&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) must not be negative&#44; and must not use CSS functions other than the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;math&#45;functions"></a>[math functions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#math-function)&#46;

The keyword <a id="valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto"></a><strong><code>auto</code></strong> is a width that is computed in <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute"></a>[parse a sizes attribute](#parse-a-sizes-attribute)&#46; If present&#44; it must be the first entry and the entire <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;list"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;list&#62;](#source-size-list) value must either be the string &#34;<code>auto</code>&#34; &#40;<a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive)&#41; or start with the string &#34;<code>auto&#44;</code>&#34; &#40;<a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive&#45;2"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive)&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

If the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element that initiated the image loading &#40;with the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;update&#45;the&#45;image&#45;data"></a>[update the image data](#update-the-image-data) or <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;img&#45;environment&#45;changes"></a>[react to environment changes](#img-environment-changes) algorithms&#41; <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;allows&#45;auto&#45;sizes"></a>[allows auto&#45;sizes](#allows-auto-sizes) and is <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;being&#45;rendered"></a>[being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#being-rendered)&#44; then <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;3"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> is the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;concrete&#45;object&#45;size"></a>[concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width&#46; If it <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;allows&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;2"></a>[allows auto&#45;sizes](#allows-auto-sizes) and is not <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;being&#45;rendered&#45;2"></a>[being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#being-rendered)&#44; but its <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;last&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;width"></a>[last auto&#45;sizes width](#last-auto-sizes-width) is not null&#44; then <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;4"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> is that width&#46; Otherwise&#44; the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;5"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> value is ignored and the next <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2) is used instead&#44; if any&#46;

The <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;6"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> keyword may be specified in the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;sizes"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-source-sizes)</code> attribute of <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> elements and <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute of <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> elements&#44; if the following conditions are met&#46; Otherwise&#44; <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;7"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> must not be specified&#46;

- The element is a <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> element with a following sibling <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46;

- The element is an <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46;

- The <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element referenced in either condition above <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;allows&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;3"></a>[allows auto&#45;sizes](#allows-auto-sizes)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

In addition&#44; it is strongly encouraged to specify dimensions using the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code> and <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;height"></a><code>[height](#attr-dim-height)</code> attributes or with CSS&#46; Without specified dimensions&#44; the image will likely render with 300x150 dimensions because <code>sizes&#61;&#34;auto&#34;</code> implies <code>contain&#45;intrinsic&#45;size&#58; 300px 150px</code> in [the Rendering section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#img-contain-size)&#46;

The <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value&#45;4"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value) gives the intended layout width of the image&#46; The author can specify different widths for different environments with <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;media&#45;condition&#45;2"></a>[&#60;media&#45;condition&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition)s&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Percentages are not allowed in a <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value&#45;5"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value)&#44; to avoid confusion about what it would be relative to&#46; The <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;&#39;vw&#39;"></a>[&#39;vw&#39;](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#vw) unit can be used for sizes relative to the <a id="sizes&#45;attributes&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width&#46;

##### <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3 Processing model[](#images-processing-model)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element has a <a id="current&#45;request"></a><strong>current request</strong> and a <a id="pending&#45;request"></a><strong>pending request</strong>&#46; The <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;request"></a>[current request](#current-request) is initially set to a new <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#46; The <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;pending&#45;request"></a>[pending request](#pending-request) is initially set to null&#46;

An <a id="image&#45;request"></a><strong>image request</strong> has a <a id="img&#45;req&#45;state"></a><strong>state</strong>&#44; <a id="img&#45;req&#45;url"></a><strong>current URL</strong>&#44; and <a id="img&#45;req&#45;data"></a><strong>image data</strong>&#46;

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;2"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;state"></a>[state](#img-req-state) is one of the following&#58;

<strong><a id="img&#45;none"></a><strong>Unavailable</strong></strong>

The user agent hasn&#39;t obtained any image data&#44; or has obtained some or all of the image data but hasn&#39;t yet decoded enough of the image to get the image dimensions&#46;

<strong><a id="img&#45;inc"></a><strong>Partially available</strong></strong>

The user agent has obtained some of the image data and at least the image dimensions are available&#46;

<strong><a id="img&#45;all"></a><strong>Completely available</strong></strong>

The user agent has obtained all of the image data and at least the image dimensions are available&#46;

<strong><a id="img&#45;error"></a><strong>Broken</strong></strong>

The user agent has obtained all of the image data that it can&#44; but it cannot even decode the image enough to get the image dimensions &#40;e&#46;g&#46; the image is corrupted&#44; or the format is not supported&#44; or no data could be obtained&#41;&#46;

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;3"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;url"></a>[current URL](#img-req-url) is initially the empty string&#46;

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;4"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;data"></a>[image data](#img-req-data) is the decoded image data&#46;

When an <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;5"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;state&#45;2"></a>[state](#img-req-state) is either <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;inc"></a>[partially available](#img-inc) or <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;all"></a>[completely available](#img-all)&#44; the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;6"></a>[image request](#image-request) is said to be <a id="img&#45;available"></a><strong>available</strong>&#46;

When an <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;request&#45;2"></a>[current request](#current-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;state&#45;3"></a>[state](#img-req-state) is <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;all&#45;2"></a>[completely available](#img-all) and the user agent can decode the media data without errors&#44; then the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element is said to be <a id="img&#45;good"></a><strong>fully decodable</strong>&#46;

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;7"></a>[image request](#image-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;req&#45;state&#45;4"></a>[state](#img-req-state) is initially <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;none"></a>[unavailable](#img-none)&#46;

When an <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;request&#45;3"></a>[current request](#current-request) is <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;img&#45;available"></a>[available](#img-available)&#44; the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element provides a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;paint&#45;source"></a>[paint source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#paint-source) whose width is the image&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;density&#45;corrected&#45;intrinsic&#45;width&#45;and&#45;height"></a>[density&#45;corrected natural width](#density-corrected-intrinsic-width-and-height) &#40;if any&#41;&#44; whose height is the image&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;density&#45;corrected&#45;intrinsic&#45;width&#45;and&#45;height&#45;2"></a>[density&#45;corrected natural height](#density-corrected-intrinsic-width-and-height) &#40;if any&#41;&#44; and whose appearance is the natural appearance of the image&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element is said to <a id="use&#45;srcset&#45;or&#45;picture"></a><strong>use <code>srcset</code> or <code>picture</code></strong> if it has a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;srcset"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-img-srcset)</code> attribute specified or if it has a parent that is a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code> element&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element has a <a id="last&#45;selected&#45;source"></a><strong>last selected source</strong>&#44; which must initially be null&#46;

Each <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element has a <a id="last&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;width"></a><strong>last auto&#45;sizes width</strong>&#44; which is a length in <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;&#39;px&#39;"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) or null&#44; initially null&#46;

Each <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;8"></a>[image request](#image-request) has a <a id="current&#45;pixel&#45;density"></a><strong>current pixel density</strong>&#44; which must initially be 1&#46;

Each <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;request&#45;9"></a>[image request](#image-request) has <a id="preferred&#45;density&#45;corrected&#45;dimensions"></a><strong>preferred density&#45;corrected dimensions</strong>&#44; which is either a struct consisting of a width and a height or is null&#46; It must initially be null&#46;

To determine the <a id="density&#45;corrected&#45;intrinsic&#45;width&#45;and&#45;height"></a><strong>density&#45;corrected natural width and height</strong> of an <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element <var>img</var>&#58;

1.  Let <var>density</var> be <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;request&#45;4"></a>[current request](#current-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;pixel&#45;density"></a>[current pixel density](#current-pixel-density)&#46;

2.  Let <var>dimensions</var> be <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;request&#45;5"></a>[current request](#current-request)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;preferred&#45;density&#45;corrected&#45;dimensions"></a>[preferred density&#45;corrected dimensions](#preferred-density-corrected-dimensions)&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    The <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;preferred&#45;density&#45;corrected&#45;dimensions&#45;2"></a>[preferred density&#45;corrected dimensions](#preferred-density-corrected-dimensions) are set in the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;prepare&#45;an&#45;image&#45;for&#45;presentation"></a>[prepare an image for presentation](#prepare-an-image-for-presentation) algorithm based on meta information in the image&#46;

3.  If <var>dimensions</var> is not null&#44; then set <var>dimensions</var>&#39;s width to <var>dimensions</var>&#39;s width divided by <var>density</var>&#44; set <var>dimensions</var>&#39;s height to <var>dimensions</var>&#39;s height divided by <var>density</var>&#44; and return <var>dimensions</var>&#46;

4.  Let <var>intrinsicWidth</var>&#44; <var>intrinsicHeight</var>&#44; and <var>intrinsicRatio</var> be <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;natural&#45;dimensions"></a>[intrinsic width&#44; intrinsic height&#44; and intrinsic aspect ratio](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions)&#44; if any&#44; respectively&#46;

5.  If <var>intrinsicWidth</var> is not absent&#44; then set <var>intrinsicWidth</var> to <var>intrinsicWidth</var> divided by <var>density</var>&#46;

6.  If <var>intrinsicHeight</var> is not absent&#44; then set <var>intrinsicHeight</var> to <var>intrinsicHeight</var> divided by <var>density</var>&#46;

7.  Return the result of applying the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;default&#45;sizing&#45;algorithm"></a>[default sizing algorithm](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing) with <var>intrinsicWidth</var>&#44; <var>intrinsicHeight</var>&#44; and <var>intrinsicRatio</var>&#44; using a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;default&#45;object&#45;size"></a>[default object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size) of 300 by 150&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

For example&#44; if the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;current&#45;pixel&#45;density&#45;2"></a>[current pixel density](#current-pixel-density) is 3&#46;125&#44; that means that there are 300 device pixels per <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;&#39;in&#39;"></a>[CSS inch](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#in)&#44; and thus if the image data is 300x600&#44; it has <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;density&#45;corrected&#45;intrinsic&#45;width&#45;and&#45;height&#45;3"></a>[density&#45;corrected natural width and height](#density-corrected-intrinsic-width-and-height) of 96 <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;&#39;px&#39;&#45;2"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) by 192 <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;&#39;px&#39;&#45;3"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)&#46;

All <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> and <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;link&#45;element"></a><code>[link](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-link-element)</code> elements are associated with a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;source&#45;set"></a>[source set](#source-set)&#46;

A <a id="source&#45;set"></a><strong>source set</strong> is an ordered set of zero or more <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;image&#45;source"></a>[image sources](#image-source) and a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2)&#46;

An <a id="image&#45;source"></a><strong>image source</strong> is a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;url"></a>[URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)&#44; and optionally either a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor)&#44; or a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;width&#45;descriptor"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor)&#46;

A <a id="source&#45;size&#45;2"></a><strong>source size</strong> is a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value)&#46; When a <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2) has a unit relative to the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#44; it must be interpreted relative to the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;11"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;node&#45;document"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;viewport&#45;2"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#46; Other units must be interpreted the same as in Media Queries&#46; [&#91;MQ&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsMQ)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A <a id="concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error"></a><strong>parse error</strong> for algorithms in this section indicates a non&#45;fatal mismatch between input and requirements&#46; User agents are encouraged to expose <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)s somehow&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Whether the image is fetched successfully or not &#40;e&#46;g&#46; whether the response status was an <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;ok&#45;status"></a>[ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status)&#41; must be ignored when determining the image&#39;s type and whether it is a valid image&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

This allows servers to return images with error responses&#44; and have them displayed&#46;

<a id="img&#45;determine&#45;type"></a>The user agent should apply the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;content&#45;type&#45;sniffing&#58;&#45;image"></a>[image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically) to determine the type of the image&#44; with the image&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;content&#45;type"></a>[associated Content&#45;Type headers](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#content-type) giving the <var>official type</var>&#46; If these rules are not applied&#44; then the type of the image must be the type given by the image&#39;s <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;content&#45;type&#45;2"></a>[associated Content&#45;Type headers](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#content-type)&#46;

User agents must not support non&#45;image resources with the <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element &#40;e&#46;g&#46; XML files whose <a id="images&#45;processing&#45;model&#58;document&#45;element"></a>[document element](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#document-element) is an HTML element&#41;&#46; User agents must not run executable code &#40;e&#46;g&#46; scripts&#41; embedded in the image resource&#46; User agents must only display the first page of a multipage resource &#40;e&#46;g&#46; a PDF file&#41;&#46; User agents must not allow the resource to act in an interactive fashion&#44; but should honour any animation in the resource&#46;

This specification does not specify which image types are to be supported&#46;

###### <a id="when&#45;to&#45;obtain&#45;images"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3&#46;1 When to obtain images[](#when-to-obtain-images)

By default&#44; images are obtained immediately&#46; User agents may provide users with the option to instead obtain them on&#45;demand&#46; &#40;The on&#45;demand option might be used by bandwidth&#45;constrained users&#44; for example&#46;&#41;

When obtaining images immediately&#44; the user agent must synchronously <a id="when&#45;to&#45;obtain&#45;images&#58;update&#45;the&#45;image&#45;data"></a>[update the image data](#update-the-image-data) of the <a id="when&#45;to&#45;obtain&#45;images&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#44; with the <em>restart animation</em> flag set if so stated&#44; whenever that element is created or has experienced <a id="when&#45;to&#45;obtain&#45;images&#58;relevant&#45;mutations"></a>[relevant mutations](#relevant-mutations)&#46;
