If <var>child</var> does not have a <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;srcset"></a><code>[srcset](#attr-source-srcset)</code> attribute&#44; <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;continue&#45;2"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue) to the next child&#46;

    4.  <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute"></a>[Parse <var>child</var>&#39;s srcset attribute](#parse-a-srcset-attribute) and let <var>source set</var> be the returned <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;source&#45;set&#45;4"></a>[source set](#source-set)&#46;

    5.  If <var>source set</var> has zero <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;image&#45;source"></a>[image sources](#image-source)&#44; <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;continue&#45;3"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue) to the next child&#46;

    6.  If <var>child</var> has a <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;media"></a><code>[media](#attr-source-media)</code> attribute&#44; and its value does not <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;matches&#45;the&#45;environment"></a>[match the environment](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#matches-the-environment)&#44; <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;continue&#45;4"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue) to the next child&#46;

    7.  <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute"></a>[Parse <var>child</var>&#39;s sizes attribute](#parse-a-sizes-attribute) with <var>img</var>&#44; and let <var>source set</var>&#39;s <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2) be the returned value&#46;

    8.  If <var>child</var> has a <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;attr&#45;source&#45;type"></a><code>[type](#attr-source-type)</code> attribute&#44; and its value is an unknown or unsupported <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;mime&#45;type"></a>[MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type)&#44; <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;continue&#45;5"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue) to the next child&#46;

    9.  If <var>child</var> has <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;width"></a><code>[width](#attr-dim-width)</code> or <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;attr&#45;dim&#45;height"></a><code>[height](#attr-dim-height)</code> attributes&#44; set <var>el</var>&#39;s <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;concept&#45;img&#45;dimension&#45;attribute&#45;source"></a>[dimension attribute source](#concept-img-dimension-attribute-source) to <var>child</var>&#46; Otherwise&#44; set <var>el</var>&#39;s <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;concept&#45;img&#45;dimension&#45;attribute&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[dimension attribute source](#concept-img-dimension-attribute-source) to <var>el</var>&#46;

    10. <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;normalise&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities"></a>[Normalize the source densities](#normalise-the-source-densities) of <var>source set</var>&#46;

    11. Set <var>el</var>&#39;s <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;source&#45;set&#45;5"></a>[source set](#source-set) to <var>source set</var>&#46;

    12. Return&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Each <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element independently considers its previous sibling <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> elements plus the <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element itself for selecting an <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;image&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[image source](#image-source)&#44; ignoring any other &#40;invalid&#41; elements&#44; including other <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> elements in the same <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;picture&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[picture](#the-picture-element)</code> element&#44; or <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;source&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[source](#the-source-element)</code> elements that are following siblings of the relevant <a id="updating&#45;the&#45;source&#45;set&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46;

###### <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3&#46;10 Parsing a srcset attribute[](#parsing-a-srcset-attribute)

When asked to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute"></a><strong>parse a srcset attribute</strong> from an element&#44; parse the value of the element&#39;s <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;srcset&#45;attribute"></a>[srcset attribute](#srcset-attribute) as follows&#58;

1.  Let <var>input</var> be the value passed to this algorithm&#46;

2.  Let <var>position</var> be a pointer into <var>input</var>&#44; initially pointing at the start of the string&#46;

3.  Let <var>candidates</var> be an initially empty <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;source&#45;set"></a>[source set](#source-set)&#46;

4.  <em>Splitting loop</em>&#58; <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace) or U&#43;002C COMMA characters from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46; If any U&#43;002C COMMA characters were collected&#44; that is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#46;

5.  If <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#44; return <var>candidates</var>&#46;

6.  <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;collect&#45;a&#45;sequence&#45;of&#45;code&#45;points&#45;2"></a>[Collect a sequence of code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#collect-a-sequence-of-code-points) that are not <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace) from <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#44; and let <var>url</var> be the result&#46;

7.  Let <var>descriptors</var> be a new empty list&#46;

8.  If <var>url</var> ends with U&#43;002C &#40;&#44;&#41;&#58;

    1.  Remove all trailing U&#43;002C COMMA characters from <var>url</var>&#46; If this removed more than one character&#44; that is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error&#45;2"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#46;

    Otherwise&#58;

    1.  <em>Descriptor tokenizer</em>&#58; <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;skip&#45;ascii&#45;whitespace"></a>[Skip ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#skip-ascii-whitespace) within <var>input</var> given <var>position</var>&#46;

    2.  Let <var>current descriptor</var> be the empty string&#46;

    3.  Let <var>state</var> be <em>in descriptor</em>&#46;

    4.  Let <var>c</var> be the character at <var>position</var>&#46; Do the following depending on the value of <var>state</var>&#46; For the purpose of this step&#44; &#34;EOF&#34; is a special character representing that <var>position</var> is past the end of <var>input</var>&#46;

        <strong><em>In descriptor</em></strong>

        Do the following&#44; depending on the value of <var>c</var>&#58;

        <strong><a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;3"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)</strong>

        If <var>current descriptor</var> is not empty&#44; append <var>current descriptor</var> to <var>descriptors</var> and let <var>current descriptor</var> be the empty string&#46; Set <var>state</var> to <em>after descriptor</em>&#46;

        <strong>U&#43;002C COMMA &#40;&#44;&#41;</strong>

        Advance <var>position</var> to the next character in <var>input</var>&#46; If <var>current descriptor</var> is not empty&#44; append <var>current descriptor</var> to <var>descriptors</var>&#46; Jump to the step labeled <em>descriptor parser</em>&#46;

        <strong>U&#43;0028 LEFT PARENTHESIS &#40;&#40;&#41;</strong>

        Append <var>c</var> to <var>current descriptor</var>&#46; Set <var>state</var> to <em>in parens</em>&#46;

        <strong>EOF</strong>

        If <var>current descriptor</var> is not empty&#44; append <var>current descriptor</var> to <var>descriptors</var>&#46; Jump to the step labeled <em>descriptor parser</em>&#46;

        <strong>Anything else</strong>

        Append <var>c</var> to <var>current descriptor</var>&#46;

        <strong><em>In parens</em></strong>

        Do the following&#44; depending on the value of <var>c</var>&#58;

        <strong>U&#43;0029 RIGHT PARENTHESIS &#40;&#41;&#41;</strong>

        Append <var>c</var> to <var>current descriptor</var>&#46; Set <var>state</var> to <em>in descriptor</em>&#46;

        <strong>EOF</strong>

        Append <var>current descriptor</var> to <var>descriptors</var>&#46; Jump to the step labeled <em>descriptor parser</em>&#46;

        <strong>Anything else</strong>

        Append <var>c</var> to <var>current descriptor</var>&#46;

        <strong><em>After descriptor</em></strong>

        Do the following&#44; depending on the value of <var>c</var>&#58;

        <strong><a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;4"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)</strong>

        Stay in this state&#46;

        <strong>EOF</strong>

        Jump to the step labeled <em>descriptor parser</em>&#46;

        <strong>Anything else</strong>

        Set <var>state</var> to <em>in descriptor</em>&#46; Set <var>position</var> to the <em>previous</em> character in <var>input</var>&#46;

        Advance <var>position</var> to the next character in <var>input</var>&#46; Repeat this step&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        In order to be compatible with future additions&#44; this algorithm supports multiple descriptors and descriptors with parens&#46;

9.  <em>Descriptor parser</em>&#58; Let <var>error</var> be <em>no</em>&#46;

10. Let <var>width</var> be <em>absent</em>&#46;

11. Let <var>density</var> be <em>absent</em>&#46;

12. Let <var>future&#45;compat&#45;h</var> be <em>absent</em>&#46;

13. For each descriptor in <var>descriptors</var>&#44; run the appropriate set of steps from the following list&#58;

    <strong>If the descriptor consists of a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer"></a>[valid non&#45;negative integer](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-non-negative-integer) followed by a U&#43;0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character</strong>

    1.  If the user agent does not support the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute&#44; let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        A conforming user agent will support the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;sizes&#45;2"></a><code>[sizes](#attr-img-sizes)</code> attribute&#46; However&#44; user agents typically implement and ship features in an incremental manner in practice&#46;

    2.  If <var>width</var> and <var>density</var> are not both <em>absent</em>&#44; then let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

    3.  Apply the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integers"></a>[rules for parsing non&#45;negative integers](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to the descriptor&#46; If the result is 0&#44; let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46; Otherwise&#44; let <var>width</var> be the result&#46;

    <strong>If the descriptor consists of a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;valid&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number"></a>[valid floating&#45;point number](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-floating-point-number) followed by a U&#43;0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character</strong>

    1.  If <var>width</var>&#44; <var>density</var> and <var>future&#45;compat&#45;h</var> are not all <em>absent</em>&#44; then let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

    2.  Apply the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;floating&#45;point&#45;number&#45;values"></a>[rules for parsing floating&#45;point number values](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-floating-point-number-values) to the descriptor&#46; If the result is less than 0&#44; let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46; Otherwise&#44; let <var>density</var> be the result&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        If <var>density</var> is 0&#44; the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;natural&#45;dimensions"></a>[natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) will be infinite&#46; User agents are [expected to have limits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#algorithm-limits) in how big images can be rendered&#46;

    <strong>If the descriptor consists of a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;valid&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integer&#45;2"></a>[valid non&#45;negative integer](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#valid-non-negative-integer) followed by a U&#43;0068 LATIN SMALL LETTER H character</strong>

    This is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error&#45;3"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#46;

    1.  If <var>future&#45;compat&#45;h</var> and <var>density</var> are not both <em>absent</em>&#44; then let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

    2.  Apply the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;rules&#45;for&#45;parsing&#45;non&#45;negative&#45;integers&#45;2"></a>[rules for parsing non&#45;negative integers](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#rules-for-parsing-non-negative-integers) to the descriptor&#46; If the result is 0&#44; let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46; Otherwise&#44; let <var>future&#45;compat&#45;h</var> be the result&#46;

    <strong>Anything else</strong>

    Let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

14. If <var>future&#45;compat&#45;h</var> is not <em>absent</em> and <var>width</var> is <em>absent</em>&#44; let <var>error</var> be <em>yes</em>&#46;

15. If <var>error</var> is still <em>no</em>&#44; then append a new <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;image&#45;source"></a>[image source](#image-source) to <var>candidates</var> whose URL is <var>url</var>&#44; associated with a width <var>width</var> if not <em>absent</em> and a pixel density <var>density</var> if not <em>absent</em>&#46; Otherwise&#44; there is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;srcset&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error&#45;4"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#46;

16. Return to the step labeled <em>splitting loop</em>&#46;

###### <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3&#46;11 Parsing a sizes attribute[](#parsing-a-sizes-attribute)

When asked to <a id="parse&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute"></a><strong>parse a sizes attribute</strong> from an element <var>element</var>&#44; with an <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element or null <var>img</var>&#58;

1.  Let <var>unparsed sizes list</var> be the result of <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;parse&#45;a&#45;comma&#45;separated&#45;list&#45;of&#45;component&#45;values"></a>[parsing a comma&#45;separated list of component values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-a-comma-separated-list-of-component-values) from the value of <var>element</var>&#39;s <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;sizes&#45;attribute"></a>[sizes attribute](#sizes-attribute) &#40;or the empty string&#44; if the attribute is absent&#41;&#46; [&#91;CSSSYNTAX&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsCSSSYNTAX)

2.  Let <var>size</var> be null&#46;

3.  For each <var>unparsed size</var> in <var>unparsed sizes list</var>&#58;

    1.  Remove all consecutive <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;whitespace&#45;token"></a>[&#60;whitespace&#45;token&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#typedef-whitespace-token)s from the end of <var>unparsed size</var>&#46; If <var>unparsed size</var> is now empty&#44; then that is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#59; <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;continue"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46;

    2.  If the last <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;component&#45;value"></a>[component value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) in <var>unparsed size</var> is a valid non&#45;negative <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value)&#44; then set <var>size</var> to its value and remove the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;component&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[component value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) from <var>unparsed size</var>&#46; Any CSS function other than the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;math&#45;functions"></a>[math functions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#math-function) is invalid&#46; Otherwise&#44; there is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error&#45;2"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#59; <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;continue&#45;2"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46;

    3.  If <var>size</var> is <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code>&#44; and <var>img</var> is not null&#44; and <var>img</var> <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;allows&#45;auto&#45;sizes"></a>[allows auto&#45;sizes](#allows-auto-sizes)&#58;

        1.  If <var>img</var> is <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;being&#45;rendered"></a>[being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#being-rendered)&#44; then set <var>size</var> to the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;concrete&#45;object&#45;size"></a>[concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width of <var>img</var>&#44; in <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;&#39;px&#39;"></a>[CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)&#44; and set <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;last&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;width"></a>[last auto&#45;sizes width](#last-auto-sizes-width) to <var>size</var>&#46;

        2.  Otherwise&#44; if <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;last&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;width&#45;2"></a>[last auto&#45;sizes width](#last-auto-sizes-width) is not null&#44; then set <var>size</var> to <var>img</var>&#39;s <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;last&#45;auto&#45;sizes&#45;width&#45;3"></a>[last auto&#45;sizes width](#last-auto-sizes-width)&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        If <var>size</var> is still <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;2"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code>&#44; then it will be ignored&#46;

    4.  Remove all consecutive <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;whitespace&#45;token&#45;2"></a>[&#60;whitespace&#45;token&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#typedef-whitespace-token)s from the end of <var>unparsed size</var>&#46; If <var>unparsed size</var> is now empty&#58;

        1.  If this was not the last item in <var>unparsed sizes list</var>&#44; that is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;concept&#45;microsyntax&#45;parse&#45;error&#45;3"></a>[parse error](#concept-microsyntax-parse-error)&#46;

        2.  If <var>size</var> is not <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;3"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code>&#44; then return <var>size</var>&#46; Otherwise&#44; continue&#46;

    5.  Parse the remaining <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;component&#45;value&#45;3"></a>[component values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) in <var>unparsed size</var> as a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;media&#45;condition"></a>[&#60;media&#45;condition&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition)&#46; If it does not parse correctly&#44; or it does parse correctly but the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;media&#45;condition&#45;2"></a>[&#60;media&#45;condition&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition) evaluates to false&#44; <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;continue&#45;3"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue)&#46; [&#91;MQ&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsMQ)

    6.  If <var>size</var> is not <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;4"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code>&#44; then return <var>size</var>&#46; Otherwise&#44; continue&#46;

4.  Return <code>100vw</code>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

It is invalid to use a bare <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;source&#45;size&#45;value&#45;2"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;value&#62;](#source-size-value) that is a <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;length&#45;2"></a>[&#60;length&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) &#40;without an accompanying <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;media&#45;condition&#45;3"></a>[&#60;media&#45;condition&#62;](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition)&#41; as an entry in the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;source&#45;size&#45;list"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;list&#62;](#source-size-list) that is not the last entry&#46; However&#44; the parsing algorithm allows it at any point in the <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;source&#45;size&#45;list&#45;2"></a>[&#60;source&#45;size&#45;list&#62;](#source-size-list)&#44; and will accept it immediately as the size if the preceding entries in the list weren&#39;t used&#46; This is to enable future extensions&#44; and protect against simple author errors such as a final trailing comma&#46; A bare <a id="parsing&#45;a&#45;sizes&#45;attribute&#58;valdef&#45;sizes&#45;auto&#45;5"></a><code>[auto](#valdef-sizes-auto)</code> keyword is allowed to have other entries following it to provide a fallback for legacy user agents&#46;

###### <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3&#46;12 Normalizing the source densities[](#normalizing-the-source-densities)

An <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source"></a>[image source](#image-source) can have a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor)&#44; a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;width&#45;descriptor"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor)&#44; or no descriptor at all accompanying its URL&#46; Normalizing a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;source&#45;set"></a>[source set](#source-set) gives every <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[image source](#image-source) a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;2"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor)&#46;

When asked to <a id="normalise&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities"></a><strong>normalize the source densities</strong> of a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;source&#45;set&#45;2"></a>[source set](#source-set) <var>source set</var>&#44; the user agent must do the following&#58;

1.  Let <var>source size</var> be <var>source set</var>&#39;s <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2)&#46;

2.  For each <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;3"></a>[image source](#image-source) in <var>source set</var>&#58;

    1.  If the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;4"></a>[image source](#image-source) has a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;3"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor)&#44; <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;continue"></a>[continue](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#iteration-continue) to the next <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;5"></a>[image source](#image-source)&#46;

    2.  Otherwise&#44; if the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;6"></a>[image source](#image-source) has a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;2"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor)&#44; replace the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;3"></a>[width descriptor](#width-descriptor) with a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;4"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor) with a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a>[value](#pixel-density-descriptor-value) of the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;width&#45;descriptor&#45;value"></a>[width descriptor value](#width-descriptor-value) divided by <var>source size</var> and a unit of <code>x</code>&#46;

        <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

        If the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;source&#45;size&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[source size](#source-size-2) is 0&#44; then the density would be infinity&#44; which results in the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;natural&#45;dimensions"></a>[natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) being 0 by 0&#46;

    3.  Otherwise&#44; give the <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;image&#45;source&#45;7"></a>[image source](#image-source) a <a id="normalizing&#45;the&#45;source&#45;densities&#58;pixel&#45;density&#45;descriptor&#45;5"></a>[pixel density descriptor](#pixel-density-descriptor) of <code>1x</code>&#46;

###### <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;3&#46;13 Reacting to environment changes[](#reacting-to-environment-changes)

The user agent may at any time run the following algorithm to update an <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s image in order to <a id="img&#45;environment&#45;changes"></a><strong>react to changes in the environment</strong>&#46; &#40;User agents are <em>not required</em> to ever run this algorithm&#59; for example&#44; if the user is not looking at the page any more&#44; the user agent might want to wait until the user has returned to the page before determining which image to use&#44; in case the environment changes again in the meantime&#46;&#41;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

User agents are encouraged to run this algorithm in particular when the user changes the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;viewport"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#39;s size &#40;e&#46;g&#46; by resizing the window or changing the page zoom&#41;&#44; and when an <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element is <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;insert&#45;an&#45;element&#45;into&#45;a&#45;document"></a>[inserted into a document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#insert-an-element-into-a-document)&#44; so that the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;density&#45;corrected&#45;intrinsic&#45;width&#45;and&#45;height"></a>[density&#45;corrected natural width and height](#density-corrected-intrinsic-width-and-height) match the new <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;viewport&#45;2"></a>[viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)&#44; and so that the correct image is chosen when <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;art&#45;direction"></a>[art direction](#art-direction) is involved&#46;

1.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;await&#45;a&#45;stable&#45;state"></a>[Await a stable state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#await-a-stable-state)&#46; The <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;synchronous&#45;section"></a>[synchronous section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#synchronous-section) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;synchronous&#45;section&#45;2"></a>[synchronous section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#synchronous-section) has ended&#46; &#40;Steps in <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;synchronous&#45;section&#45;3"></a>[synchronous sections](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#synchronous-section) are marked with ⌛&#46;&#41;

2.  ⌛ If the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element does not <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;use&#45;srcset&#45;or&#45;picture"></a>[use <code>srcset</code> or <code>picture</code>](#use-srcset-or-picture)&#44; its <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;node&#45;document"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document) is not <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;fully&#45;active"></a>[fully active](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#fully-active)&#44; it has image data whose resource type is <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;multipart&#47;x&#45;mixed&#45;replace"></a><code>[multipart&#47;x&#45;mixed&#45;replace](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#multipart/x-mixed-replace)</code>&#44; or its <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;pending&#45;request"></a>[pending request](#pending-request) is not null&#44; then return&#46;

3.  ⌛ Let <var>selected source</var> and <var>selected pixel density</var> be the URL and pixel density that results from <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;select&#45;an&#45;image&#45;source"></a>[selecting an image source](#select-an-image-source)&#44; respectively&#46;

4.  ⌛ If <var>selected source</var> is null&#44; then return&#46;

5.  ⌛ If <var>selected source</var> and <var>selected pixel density</var> are the same as the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;last&#45;selected&#45;source"></a>[last selected source](#last-selected-source) and <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;current&#45;pixel&#45;density"></a>[current pixel density](#current-pixel-density)&#44; then return&#46;

6.  ⌛ Let <var>urlString</var> be the result of <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;encoding&#45;parsing&#45;and&#45;serializing&#45;a&#45;url"></a>[encoding&#45;parsing&#45;and&#45;serializing a URL](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#encoding-parsing-and-serializing-a-url) given <var>selected source</var>&#44; relative to the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;node&#45;document&#45;2"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#46;

7.  ⌛ If <var>urlString</var> is failure&#44; then return&#46;

8.  ⌛ Let <var>corsAttributeState</var> be the state of the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;crossorigin"></a><code>[crossorigin](#attr-img-crossorigin)</code> content attribute&#46;

9.  ⌛ Let <var>origin</var> be the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;node&#45;document&#45;3"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;origin"></a>[origin](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin)&#46;

10. ⌛ Let <var>client</var> be the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;node&#45;document&#45;4"></a>[node document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-document)&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;relevant&#45;settings&#45;object"></a>[relevant settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#relevant-settings-object)&#46;

11. ⌛ Let <var>key</var> be a tuple consisting of <var>urlString</var>&#44; <var>corsAttributeState</var>&#44; and&#44; if <var>corsAttributeState</var> is not <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;attr&#45;crossorigin&#45;none"></a>[No CORS](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#attr-crossorigin-none)&#44; <var>origin</var>&#46;

12. ⌛ Let <var>image request</var> be a new <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;image&#45;request"></a>[image request](#image-request) whose <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;img&#45;req&#45;url"></a>[current URL](#img-req-url) is <var>urlString</var>&#46;

13. ⌛ Set the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;pending&#45;request&#45;2"></a>[pending request](#pending-request) to <var>image request</var>&#46;

14. End the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;synchronous&#45;section&#45;4"></a>[synchronous section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#synchronous-section)&#44; continuing the remaining steps <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;in&#45;parallel"></a>[in parallel](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#in-parallel)&#46;

15. Let <var>finishUpdate</var> be the following steps&#58;

    1.  If the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element has experienced <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;relevant&#45;mutations"></a>[relevant mutations](#relevant-mutations) since this algorithm started&#44; then set the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;pending&#45;request&#45;3"></a>[pending request](#pending-request) to null and abort these steps&#46;

    2.  Set the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;last&#45;selected&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[last selected source](#last-selected-source) to <var>selected source</var> and the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;current&#45;pixel&#45;density&#45;2"></a>[current pixel density](#current-pixel-density) to <var>selected pixel density</var>&#46;

    3.  Set the <var>image request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;img&#45;req&#45;state"></a>[state](#img-req-state) to <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;img&#45;all"></a>[completely available](#img-all)&#46;

    4.  Add the image to the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;list&#45;of&#45;available&#45;images"></a>[list of available images](#list-of-available-images) using the key <var>key</var>&#44; with the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;ignore&#45;higher&#45;layer&#45;caching"></a>[ignore higher&#45;layer caching](#ignore-higher-layer-caching) flag set&#46;

    5.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;upgrade&#45;the&#45;pending&#45;request&#45;to&#45;the&#45;current&#45;request"></a>[Upgrade the pending request to the current request](#upgrade-the-pending-request-to-the-current-request)&#46;

    6.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;prepare&#45;an&#45;image&#45;for&#45;presentation"></a>[Prepare <var>image request</var> for presentation](#prepare-an-image-for-presentation) given the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46;

    7.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;event&#45;fire"></a>[Fire an event](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-fire) named <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;event&#45;load"></a><code>[load](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-load)</code> at the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;10"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46;

16. If the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;list&#45;of&#45;available&#45;images&#45;2"></a>[list of available images](#list-of-available-images) contains an entry for <var>key</var>&#58;

    1.  Set <var>image request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;img&#45;req&#45;data"></a>[image data](#img-req-data) to that of the entry&#46;

    2.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;queue&#45;an&#45;element&#45;task"></a>[Queue an element task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-an-element-task) on the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;11"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element and <var>finishUpdate</var>&#46;

17. Otherwise&#58;

    1.  Let <var>request</var> be the result of <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;create&#45;a&#45;potential&#45;cors&#45;request"></a>[creating a potential&#45;CORS request](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#create-a-potential-cors-request) given <var>urlString</var>&#44; &#34;<code>image</code>&#34;&#44; and <var>corsAttributeState</var>&#46;

    2.  Set <var>request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;request&#45;client"></a>[client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to <var>client</var> and set <var>request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;request&#45;initiator"></a>[initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) to &#34;<code>imageset</code>&#34;&#46;

    3.  Set <var>request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;request&#45;referrer&#45;policy"></a>[referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to the current state of the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;referrerpolicy"></a><code>[referrerpolicy](#attr-img-referrerpolicy)</code> attribute&#46;

    4.  Set <var>request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;request&#45;priority"></a>[priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to the current state of the element&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;fetchpriority"></a><code>[fetchpriority](#attr-img-fetchpriority)</code> attribute&#46;

    5.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;fetch"></a>[Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) <var>request</var>&#44; with <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;processresponse"></a><em>[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)</em> set to the following steps given <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;concept&#45;response"></a>[response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) <var>response</var>&#58;

        1.  If <var>response</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;unsafe&#45;response"></a>[unsafe response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#unsafe-response) is a <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;network&#45;error"></a>[network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error) or if the image format is unsupported &#40;as determined by applying the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;content&#45;type&#45;sniffing&#58;&#45;image"></a>[image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically)&#44; again as mentioned earlier&#41;&#44; or if the user agent is able to determine that <var>image request</var>&#39;s image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained&#44; or if the resource type is <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;multipart&#47;x&#45;mixed&#45;replace&#45;2"></a><code>[multipart&#47;x&#45;mixed&#45;replace](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#multipart/x-mixed-replace)</code>&#44; then set the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;pending&#45;request&#45;4"></a>[pending request](#pending-request) to null and return&#46;

        2.  Otherwise&#44; <var>response</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;unsafe&#45;response&#45;2"></a>[unsafe response](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#unsafe-response) is <var>image request</var>&#39;s <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;img&#45;req&#45;data&#45;2"></a>[image data](#img-req-data)&#46; It can be either <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;cors&#45;same&#45;origin"></a>[CORS&#45;same&#45;origin](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#cors-same-origin) or <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;cors&#45;cross&#45;origin"></a>[CORS&#45;cross&#45;origin](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#cors-cross-origin)&#59; this affects the image&#39;s interaction with other APIs &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; when used on a <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;canvas&#45;element"></a><code>[canvas](html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-canvas-element)</code>&#41;&#46;

        3.  <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;queue&#45;an&#45;element&#45;task&#45;2"></a>[Queue an element task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#queue-an-element-task) on the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;dom&#45;manipulation&#45;task&#45;source&#45;2"></a>[DOM manipulation task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-manipulation-task-source) given the <a id="reacting&#45;to&#45;environment&#45;changes&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element and <var>finishUpdate</var>&#46;

##### <a id="alt"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4 Requirements for providing text to act as an alternative for images[](#alt)

###### <a id="general&#45;guidelines"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;1 General guidelines[](#general-guidelines)

Except where otherwise specified&#44; the <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be specified and its value must not be empty&#59; the value must be an appropriate replacement for the image&#46; The specific requirements for the <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;2"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute depend on what the image is intended to represent&#44; as described in the following sections&#46;

The most general rule to consider when writing alternative text is the following&#58; <strong>the intent is that replacing every image with the text of its <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;3"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute does not change the meaning of the page</strong>&#46;

So&#44; in general&#44; alternative text can be written by considering what one would have written had one not been able to include the image&#46;

A corollary to this is that the <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;4"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#39;s value should never contain text that could be considered the image&#39;s <em>caption</em>&#44; <em>title</em>&#44; or <em>legend</em>&#46; It is supposed to contain replacement text that could be used by users <em>instead</em> of the image&#59; it is not meant to supplement the image&#46; The <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute can be used for supplemental information&#46;

Another corollary is that the <a id="general&#45;guidelines&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;5"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#39;s value should not repeat information that is already provided in the prose next to the image&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

One way to think of alternative text is to think about how you would read the page containing the image to someone over the phone&#44; without mentioning that there is an image present&#46; Whatever you say instead of the image is typically a good start for writing the alternative text&#46;

###### <a id="a&#45;link&#45;or&#45;button&#45;containing&#45;nothing&#45;but&#45;the&#45;image"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;2 A link or button containing nothing but the image[](#a-link-or-button-containing-nothing-but-the-image)

When an <a id="a&#45;link&#45;or&#45;button&#45;containing&#45;nothing&#45;but&#45;the&#45;image&#58;the&#45;a&#45;element"></a><code>[a](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-a-element)</code> element that creates a <a id="a&#45;link&#45;or&#45;button&#45;containing&#45;nothing&#45;but&#45;the&#45;image&#58;hyperlink"></a>[hyperlink](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#hyperlink)&#44; or a <a id="a&#45;link&#45;or&#45;button&#45;containing&#45;nothing&#45;but&#45;the&#45;image&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> element&#44; has no textual content but contains one or more images&#44; the <a id="a&#45;link&#45;or&#45;button&#45;containing&#45;nothing&#45;but&#45;the&#45;image&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attributes must contain text that together convey the purpose of the link or button&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example&#44; a user is asked to pick their preferred color from a list of three&#46; Each color is given by an image&#44; but for users who have configured their user agent not to display images&#44; the color names are used instead&#58;

``` text
<h1>Pick your color</h1>
<ul>
 <li><a href="green.html"><img src="green.jpeg" alt="Green"></a></li>
 <li><a href="blue.html"><img src="blue.jpeg" alt="Blue"></a></li>
 <li><a href="red.html"><img src="red.jpeg" alt="Red"></a></li>
</ul>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example&#44; each button has a set of images to indicate the kind of color output desired by the user&#46; The first image is used in each case to give the alternative text&#46;

``` text
<button name="rgb"><img src="red" alt="RGB"><img src="green" alt=""><img src="blue" alt=""></button>
<button name="cmyk"><img src="cyan" alt="CMYK"><img src="magenta" alt=""><img src="yellow" alt=""><img src="black" alt=""></button>
```

Since each image represents one part of the text&#44; it could also be written like this&#58;

``` text
<button name="rgb"><img src="red" alt="R"><img src="green" alt="G"><img src="blue" alt="B"></button>
<button name="cmyk"><img src="cyan" alt="C"><img src="magenta" alt="M"><img src="yellow" alt="Y"><img src="black" alt="K"></button>
```

However&#44; with other alternative text&#44; this might not work&#44; and putting all the alternative text into one image in each case might make more sense&#58;

``` text
<button name="rgb"><img src="red" alt="sRGB profile"><img src="green" alt=""><img src="blue" alt=""></button>
<button name="cmyk"><img src="cyan" alt="CMYK profile"><img src="magenta" alt=""><img src="yellow" alt=""><img src="black" alt=""></button>
```

###### <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;3 A phrase or paragraph with an alternative graphical representation&#58; charts&#44; diagrams&#44; graphs&#44; maps&#44; illustrations[](#a-phrase-or-paragraph-with-an-alternative-graphical-representation:-charts,-diagrams,-graphs,-maps,-illustrations)

Sometimes something can be more clearly stated in graphical form&#44; for example as a flowchart&#44; a diagram&#44; a graph&#44; or a simple map showing directions&#46; In such cases&#44; an image can be given using the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#44; but the lesser textual version must still be given&#44; so that users who are unable to view the image &#40;e&#46;g&#46; because they have a very slow connection&#44; or because they are using a text&#45;only browser&#44; or because they are listening to the page being read out by a hands&#45;free automobile voice web browser&#44; or simply because they are blind&#41; are still able to understand the message being conveyed&#46;

The text must be given in the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#44; and must convey the same message as the image specified in the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;src"></a><code>[src](#attr-img-src)</code> attribute&#46;

It is important to realize that the alternative text is a <em>replacement</em> for the image&#44; not a description of the image&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example we have [a flowchart](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/parsing-model-overview.svg) in image form&#44; with text in the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;2"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute rephrasing the flowchart in prose form&#58;

``` text
<p>In the common case, the data handled by the tokenization stage
comes from the network, but it can also come from script.</p>
<p><img src="images/parsing-model-overview.svg" alt="The Network
passes data to the Input Stream Preprocessor, which passes it to the
Tokenizer, which passes it to the Tree Construction stage. From there,
data goes to both the DOM and to Script Execution. Script Execution is
linked to the DOM, and, using document.write(), passes data to the
Tokenizer."></p>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here&#39;s another example&#44; showing a good solution and a bad solution to the problem of including an image in a description&#46;

First&#44; here&#39;s the good solution&#46; This sample shows how the alternative text should just be what you would have put in the prose if the image had never existed&#46;

``` text
<!-- This is the correct way to do things. -->
<p>
 You are standing in an open field west of a house.
 <img src="house.jpeg" alt="The house is white, with a boarded front door.">
 There is a small mailbox here.
</p>
```

Second&#44; here&#39;s the bad solution&#46; In this incorrect way of doing things&#44; the alternative text is simply a description of the image&#44; instead of a textual replacement for the image&#46; It&#39;s bad because when the image isn&#39;t shown&#44; the text doesn&#39;t flow as well as in the first example&#46;

``` text
<!-- This is the wrong way to do things. -->
<p>
 You are standing in an open field west of a house.
 <img src="house.jpeg" alt="A white house, with a boarded front door.">
 There is a small mailbox here.
</p>
```

Text such as &#34;Photo of white house with boarded door&#34; would be equally bad alternative text &#40;though it could be suitable for the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute or in the <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;the&#45;figcaption&#45;element"></a><code>[figcaption](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figcaption-element)</code> element of a <a id="a&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;paragraph&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;charts&#44;&#45;diagrams&#44;&#45;graphs&#44;&#45;maps&#44;&#45;illustrations&#58;the&#45;figure&#45;element"></a><code>[figure](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figure-element)</code> with this image&#41;&#46;

###### <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;4 A short phrase or label with an alternative graphical representation&#58; icons&#44; logos[](#a-short-phrase-or-label-with-an-alternative-graphical-representation:-icons,-logos)

A document can contain information in iconic form&#46; The icon is intended to help users of visual browsers to recognize features at a glance&#46;

In some cases&#44; the icon is supplemental to a text label conveying the same meaning&#46; In those cases&#44; the <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be present but must be empty&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here the icons are next to text that conveys the same meaning&#44; so they have an empty <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;2"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#58;

``` text
<nav>
 <p><a href="/help/"><img src="/icons/help.png" alt=""> Help</a></p>
 <p><a href="/configure/"><img src="/icons/configuration.png" alt="">
 Configuration Tools</a></p>
</nav>
```

In other cases&#44; the icon has no text next to it describing what it means&#59; the icon is supposed to be self&#45;explanatory&#46; In those cases&#44; an equivalent textual label must be given in the <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;3"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Here&#44; posts on a news site are labeled with an icon indicating their topic&#46;

``` text
<body>
 <article>
  <header>
   <h1>Ratatouille wins <i>Best Movie of the Year</i> award</h1>
   <p><img src="movies.png" alt="Movies"></p>
  </header>
  <p>Pixar has won yet another <i>Best Movie of the Year</i> award,
  making this its 8th win in the last 12 years.</p>
 </article>
 <article>
  <header>
   <h1>Latest TWiT episode is online</h1>
   <p><img src="podcasts.png" alt="Podcasts"></p>
  </header>
  <p>The latest TWiT episode has been posted, in which we hear
  several tech news stories as well as learning much more about the
  iPhone. This week, the panelists compare how reflective their
  iPhones' Apple logos are.</p>
 </article>
</body>
```

Many pages include logos&#44; insignia&#44; flags&#44; or emblems&#44; which stand for a particular entity such as a company&#44; organization&#44; project&#44; band&#44; software package&#44; country&#44; or some such&#46;

If the logo is being used to represent the entity&#44; e&#46;g&#46; as a page heading&#44; the <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;4"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must contain the name of the entity being represented by the logo&#46; The <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;5"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must <em>not</em> contain text like the word &#34;logo&#34;&#44; as it is not the fact that it is a logo that is being conveyed&#44; it&#39;s the entity itself&#46;

If the logo is being used next to the name of the entity that it represents&#44; then the logo is supplemental&#44; and its <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;6"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must instead be empty&#46;

If the logo is merely used as decorative material &#40;as branding&#44; or&#44; for example&#44; as a side image in an article that mentions the entity to which the logo belongs&#41;&#44; then the entry below on purely decorative images applies&#46; If the logo is actually being discussed&#44; then it is being used as a phrase or paragraph &#40;the description of the logo&#41; with an alternative graphical representation &#40;the logo itself&#41;&#44; and the first entry above applies&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following snippets&#44; all four of the above cases are present&#46; First&#44; we see a logo used to represent a company&#58;

``` text
<h1><img src="XYZ.gif" alt="The XYZ company"></h1>
```

Next&#44; we see a paragraph which uses a logo right next to the company name&#44; and so doesn&#39;t have any alternative text&#58;

``` text
<article>
 <h2>News</h2>
 <p>We have recently been looking at buying the <img src="alpha.gif"
 alt=""> ΑΒΓ company, a small Greek company
 specializing in our type of product.</p>
```

In this third snippet&#44; we have a logo being used in an aside&#44; as part of the larger article discussing the acquisition&#58;

``` text
<aside><p><img src="alpha-large.gif" alt=""></p></aside>
 <p>The ΑΒΓ company has had a good quarter, and our
 pie chart studies of their accounts suggest a much bigger blue slice
 than its green and orange slices, which is always a good sign.</p>
</article>
```

Finally&#44; we have an opinion piece talking about a logo&#44; and the logo is therefore described in detail in the alternative text&#46;

``` text
<p>Consider for a moment their logo:</p>

<p><img src="/images/logo" alt="It consists of a green circle with a
green question mark centered inside it."></p>

<p>How unoriginal can you get? I mean, oooooh, a question mark, how
<em>revolutionary</em>, how utterly <em>ground-breaking</em>, I'm
sure everyone will rush to adopt those specifications now! They could
at least have tried for some sort of, I don't know, sequence of
rounded squares with varying shades of green and bold white outlines,
at least that would look good on the cover of a blue book.</p>
```

This example shows how the alternative text should be written such that if the image isn&#39;t <a id="a&#45;short&#45;phrase&#45;or&#45;label&#45;with&#45;an&#45;alternative&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#58;&#45;icons&#44;&#45;logos&#58;img&#45;available"></a><em>[available](#img-available)</em>&#44; and the text is used instead&#44; the text flows seamlessly into the surrounding text&#44; as if the image had never been there in the first place&#46;

###### <a id="text&#45;that&#45;has&#45;been&#45;rendered&#45;to&#45;a&#45;graphic&#45;for&#45;typographical&#45;effect"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;5 Text that has been rendered to a graphic for typographical effect[](#text-that-has-been-rendered-to-a-graphic-for-typographical-effect)

Sometimes&#44; an image just consists of text&#44; and the purpose of the image is not to highlight the actual typographic effects used to render the text&#44; but just to convey the text itself&#46;

In such cases&#44; the <a id="text&#45;that&#45;has&#45;been&#45;rendered&#45;to&#45;a&#45;graphic&#45;for&#45;typographical&#45;effect&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be present but must consist of the same text as written in the image itself&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Consider a graphic containing the text &#34;Earth Day&#34;&#44; but with the letters all decorated with flowers and plants&#46; If the text is merely being used as a heading&#44; to spice up the page for graphical users&#44; then the correct alternative text is just the same text &#34;Earth Day&#34;&#44; and no mention need be made of the decorations&#58;

``` text
<h1><img src="earthdayheading.png" alt="Earth Day"></h1>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

An illuminated manuscript might use graphics for some of its images&#46; The alternative text in such a situation is just the character that the image represents&#46;

``` text
<p><img src="initials/o.svg" alt="O">nce upon a time and a long long time ago, late at
night, when it was dark, over the hills, through the woods, across a great ocean, in a land far
away, in a small house, on a hill, under a full moon...
```

When an image is used to represent a character that cannot otherwise be represented in Unicode&#44; for example gaiji&#44; itaiji&#44; or new characters such as novel currency symbols&#44; the alternative text should be a more conventional way of writing the same thing&#44; e&#46;g&#46; using the phonetic hiragana or katakana to give the character&#39;s pronunciation&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In this example from 1997&#44; a new&#45;fangled currency symbol that looks like a curly E with two bars in the middle instead of one is represented using an image&#46; The alternative text gives the character&#39;s pronunciation&#46;

``` text
<p>Only <img src="euro.png" alt="euro ">5.99!
```

An image should not be used if characters would serve an identical purpose&#46; Only when the text cannot be directly represented using text&#44; e&#46;g&#46;&#44; because of decorations or because there is no appropriate character &#40;as in the case of gaiji&#41;&#44; would an image be appropriate&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

If an author is tempted to use an image because their default system font does not support a given character&#44; then web fonts are a better solution than images&#46;

###### <a id="a&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;some&#45;of&#45;the&#45;surrounding&#45;text"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;6 A graphical representation of some of the surrounding text[](#a-graphical-representation-of-some-of-the-surrounding-text)

In many cases&#44; the image is actually just supplementary&#44; and its presence merely reinforces the surrounding text&#46; In these cases&#44; the <a id="a&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;some&#45;of&#45;the&#45;surrounding&#45;text&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be present but its value must be the empty string&#46;

In general&#44; an image falls into this category if removing the image doesn&#39;t make the page any less useful&#44; but including the image makes it a lot easier for users of visual browsers to understand the concept&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A flowchart that repeats the previous paragraph in graphical form&#58;

``` text
<p>The Network passes data to the Input Stream Preprocessor, which
passes it to the Tokenizer, which passes it to the Tree Construction
stage. From there, data goes to both the DOM and to Script Execution.
Script Execution is linked to the DOM, and, using document.write(),
passes data to the Tokenizer.</p>
<p><img src="images/parsing-model-overview.svg" alt=""></p>
```

In these cases&#44; it would be wrong to include alternative text that consists of just a caption&#46; If a caption is to be included&#44; then either the <a id="a&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;some&#45;of&#45;the&#45;surrounding&#45;text&#58;attr&#45;title"></a><code>[title](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-title)</code> attribute can be used&#44; or the <a id="a&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;some&#45;of&#45;the&#45;surrounding&#45;text&#58;the&#45;figure&#45;element"></a><code>[figure](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figure-element)</code> and <a id="a&#45;graphical&#45;representation&#45;of&#45;some&#45;of&#45;the&#45;surrounding&#45;text&#58;the&#45;figcaption&#45;element"></a><code>[figcaption](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-figcaption-element)</code> elements can be used&#46; In the latter case&#44; the image would in fact be a phrase or paragraph with an alternative graphical representation&#44; and would thus require alternative text&#46;

``` text
<!-- Using the title="" attribute -->
<p>The Network passes data to the Input Stream Preprocessor, which
passes it to the Tokenizer, which passes it to the Tree Construction
stage. From there, data goes to both the DOM and to Script Execution.
Script Execution is linked to the DOM, and, using document.write(),
passes data to the Tokenizer.</p>
<p><img src="images/parsing-model-overview.svg" alt=""
        title="Flowchart representation of the parsing model."></p>
```

``` text
<!-- Using <figure> and <figcaption> -->
<p>The Network passes data to the Input Stream Preprocessor, which
passes it to the Tokenizer, which passes it to the Tree Construction
stage. From there, data goes to both the DOM and to Script Execution.
Script Execution is linked to the DOM, and, using document.write(),
passes data to the Tokenizer.</p>
<figure>
 <img src="images/parsing-model-overview.svg" alt="The Network leads to
 the Input Stream Preprocessor, which leads to the Tokenizer, which
 leads to the Tree Construction stage. The Tree Construction stage
 leads to two items. The first is Script Execution, which leads via
 document.write() back to the Tokenizer. The second item from which
 Tree Construction leads is the DOM. The DOM is related to the Script
 Execution.">
 <figcaption>Flowchart representation of the parsing model.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

``` text
<!-- This is WRONG. Do not do this. Instead, do what the above examples do. -->
<p>The Network passes data to the Input Stream Preprocessor, which
passes it to the Tokenizer, which passes it to the Tree Construction
stage. From there, data goes to both the DOM and to Script Execution.
Script Execution is linked to the DOM, and, using document.write(),
passes data to the Tokenizer.</p>
<p><img src="images/parsing-model-overview.svg"
        alt="Flowchart representation of the parsing model."></p>
<!-- Never put the image's caption in the alt="" attribute! -->
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

A graph that repeats the previous paragraph in graphical form&#58;

``` text
<p>According to a study covering several billion pages,
about 62% of documents on the web in 2007 triggered the Quirks
rendering mode of web browsers, about 30% triggered the Almost
Standards mode, and about 9% triggered the Standards mode.</p>
<p><img src="rendering-mode-pie-chart.png" alt=""></p>
```

###### <a id="ancillary&#45;images"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;7 Ancillary images[](#ancillary-images)

Sometimes&#44; an image is not critical to the content&#44; but is nonetheless neither purely decorative nor entirely redundant with the text&#46; In these cases&#44; the <a id="ancillary&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be present&#44; and its value should either be the empty string&#44; or a textual representation of the information that the image conveys&#46; If the image has a caption giving the image&#39;s title&#44; then the <a id="ancillary&#45;images&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;2"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute&#39;s value must not be empty &#40;as that would be quite confusing for non&#45;visual readers&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Consider a news article about a political figure&#44; in which the individual&#39;s face was shown in an image&#46; The image is not purely decorative&#44; as it is relevant to the story&#46; The image is not entirely redundant with the story either&#44; as it shows what the politician looks like&#46; Whether any alternative text need be provided is an authoring decision&#44; decided by whether the image influences the interpretation of the prose&#46;

In this first variant&#44; the image is shown without context&#44; and no alternative text is provided&#58;

``` text
<p><img src="president.jpeg" alt=""> Ahead of today's referendum,
the President wrote an open letter to all registered voters. In it, she admitted that the country was
divided.</p>
```

If the picture is just a face&#44; there might be no value in describing it&#46; It&#39;s of no interest to the reader whether the individual has red hair or blond hair&#44; whether the individual has white skin or black skin&#44; whether the individual has one eye or two eyes&#46;

However&#44; if the picture is more dynamic&#44; for instance showing the politician as angry&#44; or particularly happy&#44; or devastated&#44; some alternative text would be useful in setting the tone of the article&#44; a tone that might otherwise be missed&#58;

``` text
<p><img src="president.jpeg" alt="The President is sad.">
Ahead of today's referendum, the President wrote an open letter to all
registered voters. In it, she admitted that the country was divided.
</p>
```

``` text
<p><img src="president.jpeg" alt="The President is happy!">
Ahead of today's referendum, the President wrote an open letter to all
registered voters. In it, she admitted that the country was divided.
</p>
```

Whether the individual was &#34;sad&#34; or &#34;happy&#34; makes a difference to how the rest of the paragraph is to be interpreted&#58; is she likely saying that she is unhappy with the country being divided&#44; or is she saying that the prospect of a divided country is good for her political career&#63; The interpretation varies based on the image&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

If the image has a caption&#44; then including alternative text avoids leaving the non&#45;visual user confused as to what the caption refers to&#46;

``` text
<p>Ahead of today's referendum, the President wrote an open letter to
all registered voters. In it, she admitted that the country was divided.</p>
<figure>
 <img src="president.jpeg"
      alt="A high forehead, cheerful disposition, and dark hair round out the President's face.">
 <figcaption> The President of Ruritania. Photo © 2014 PolitiPhoto. </figcaption>
</figure>
```

###### <a id="a&#45;purely&#45;decorative&#45;image&#45;that&#45;doesn&#39;t&#45;add&#45;any&#45;information"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;8 A purely decorative image that doesn&#39;t add any information[](#a-purely-decorative-image-that-doesn't-add-any-information)

If an image is decorative but isn&#39;t especially page&#45;specific — for example an image that forms part of a site&#45;wide design scheme — the image should be specified in the site&#39;s CSS&#44; not in the markup of the document&#46;

However&#44; a decorative image that isn&#39;t discussed by the surrounding text but still has some relevance can be included in a page using the <a id="a&#45;purely&#45;decorative&#45;image&#45;that&#45;doesn&#39;t&#45;add&#45;any&#45;information&#58;the&#45;img&#45;element"></a><code>[img](#the-img-element)</code> element&#46; Such images are decorative&#44; but still form part of the content&#46; In these cases&#44; the <a id="a&#45;purely&#45;decorative&#45;image&#45;that&#45;doesn&#39;t&#45;add&#45;any&#45;information&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute must be present but its value must be the empty string&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Examples where the image is purely decorative despite being relevant would include things like a photo of the Black Rock City landscape in a blog post about an event at Burning Man&#44; or an image of a painting inspired by a poem&#44; on a page reciting that poem&#46; The following snippet shows an example of the latter case &#40;only the first verse is included in this snippet&#41;&#58;

``` text
<h1>The Lady of Shalott</h1>
<p><img src="shalott.jpeg" alt=""></p>
<p>On either side the river lie<br>
Long fields of barley and of rye,<br>
That clothe the wold and meet the sky;<br>
And through the field the road run by<br>
To many-tower'd Camelot;<br>
And up and down the people go,<br>
Gazing where the lilies blow<br>
Round an island there below,<br>
The island of Shalott.</p>
```

###### <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;no&#45;links"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;9 A group of images that form a single larger picture with no links[](#a-group-of-images-that-form-a-single-larger-picture-with-no-links)

When a picture has been sliced into smaller image files that are then displayed together to form the complete picture again&#44; one of the images must have its <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;no&#45;links&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute set as per the relevant rules that would be appropriate for the picture as a whole&#44; and then all the remaining images must have their <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;no&#45;links&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt&#45;2"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute set to the empty string&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; a picture representing a company logo for XYZ Corp has been split into two pieces&#44; the first containing the letters &#34;XYZ&#34; and the second with the word &#34;Corp&#34;&#46; The alternative text &#40;&#34;XYZ Corp&#34;&#41; is all in the first image&#46;

``` text
<h1><img src="logo1.png" alt="XYZ Corp"><img src="logo2.png" alt=""></h1>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; a rating is shown as three filled stars and two empty stars&#46; While the alternative text could have been &#34;★★★☆☆&#34;&#44; the author has instead decided to more helpfully give the rating in the form &#34;3 out of 5&#34;&#46; That is the alternative text of the first image&#44; and the rest have blank alternative text&#46;

``` text
<p>Rating: <meter max=5 value=3><img src="1" alt="3 out of 5"
  ><img src="1" alt=""><img src="1" alt=""><img src="0" alt=""
  ><img src="0" alt=""></meter></p>
```

###### <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;links"></a>4&#46;8&#46;4&#46;4&#46;10 A group of images that form a single larger picture with links[](#a-group-of-images-that-form-a-single-larger-picture-with-links)

Generally&#44; <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;links&#58;image&#45;map"></a>[image maps](#image-map) should be used instead of slicing an image for links&#46;

However&#44; if an image is indeed sliced and any of the components of the sliced picture are the sole contents of links&#44; then one image per link must have alternative text in its <a id="a&#45;group&#45;of&#45;images&#45;that&#45;form&#45;a&#45;single&#45;larger&#45;picture&#45;with&#45;links&#58;attr&#45;img&#45;alt"></a><code>[alt](#attr-img-alt)</code> attribute representing the purpose of the link&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; a picture representing the flying spaghetti monster emblem&#44; with each of the left noodly appendages and the right noodly appendages in different images&#44; so that the user can pick the left side or the right side in an adventure&#46;

``` text
<h1>The Church</h1>
<p>You come across a flying spaghetti monster. Which side of His
Noodliness do you wish to reach out for?</p>
<p><a href="?go=left" ><img src="fsm-left.png"  alt="Left side. "></a
  ><img src="fsm-middle.png" alt=""
```
